rationale.usefulness: The intent map, implication-versus-converse login example and explicit trusted boundary provide concrete learning and review techniques. The proposed permission-rule exercise is actionable separately, but the integrated PDD workflow is not established as publicly installable.
rationale.impact: The evidence establishes one reported login slice, not a scalable assurance system or a replicated improvement over existing verification practice. Connecting agent planning to machine-checked obligations has credible potential, but demonstrated significance remains a bounded research contribution.
rationale.novelty: The distinctive element is the integration of human intent decisions, specification links, mutation checks and proof/test reporting. Formal specifications and Verus proofs are established component ideas; no comparative evidence establishes a new verification capability.
rationale.maturity: Microsoft explicitly calls PDD Kit a Rust research prototype. Chopin discourages use and Verus warns of incomplete features/documentation. A reported application example supports more than speculation, but availability, setup reproducibility and reliability of the integrated toolkit remain unverified.
rationale.openness: The article exposes the process and its assumptions and links publicly inspectable component projects. It does not establish a complete PDD distribution, license or reproducible example package, so component openness cannot be credited to the integrated kit.

concerns: The integrated toolkit remains unavailable as a verified reproducible public package; the report clearly retains this boundary. No publication-blocking factual or safety issue found.
